findings.title: Any successful tool call is treated as evidence of diff coverage
findings.description: The cap is skipped after any successful tool call, but the design does not establish that the call read a relevant file—or that its result covered the omitted diff. For example, a successful `Glob` or a read of an unrelated file can leave a truncated review eligible for a clean PASS. That falls short of the stated goal that a PASS means the model saw the whole diff or read the relevant content with tools. Only treat calls that provide relevant file content as coverage evidence; if coverage cannot be established, keep the result from being a clean PASS.

findings.title: The total-injection-limit case can receive a false truncation explanation
findings.description: D3 records only the total and injected character counts when the total-injection limit skips the diff. But D4’s synthetic-finding example attributes the omission to `review.max_file_size_bytes`. For a diff skipped by the total-injection limit, that explanation is inaccurate; the design does not specify a cause-neutral message or retain enough information to name the actual cause. Make the finding accurate for both truncation paths, either by using cause-neutral wording or by recording the cause.
